title: Automata Forge
description: A from-scratch theory-of-computation lab spanning the WHOLE Chomsky hierarchy AND the temporal logic above it. NEWEST — v16 PROBABILISTIC mode, a complete from-scratch PROBABILISTIC MODEL CHECKER — the QUANTITATIVE counterpart to the lab's qualitative CTL/LTL engines, and the theory behind PRISM/Storm. It reasons about DISCRETE-TIME MARKOV CHAINS (each state carries ONE probability distribution over successors) and MARKOV DECISION PROCESSES (each state a menu of ACTIONS, so a controller plays a game against chance), checked with PCTL (Probabilistic CTL): the qualitative operator P⋈p[ψ] and the value query P=?[ψ] over path formulas X, U, F, G with optional step bounds <=k, the long-run operator S=?[φ], and Pmax/Pmin over ALL schedulers for MDPs. The headline is EXACTNESS: unbounded reachability P(F ψ) is not a limit to approximate — it is the exact solution of the linear system (I−P)x=b over the 'maybe' states, solved in EXACT BigInt RATIONALS by Gauss–Jordan, so the KNUTH–YAO die (a fair d6 from fair coin flips) yields each face at exactly 1/6 with 11/3 flips expected, CRAPS comes out 244/495, the GAMBLER'S RUIN i/N, and a two-state weather chain's steady state 2/7 — no floating-point dust. Step-bounded properties are exact matrix iteration; MDP optima come from value iteration AND exact Howard POLICY ITERATION (evaluate a policy by a rational linear solve, improve by exact one-step look-ahead); the long run comes from the STATIONARY distributions of the chain's bottom SCCs. A forgiving textual model syntax (dtmc/mdp, init, s -> 1/2: a, 1/2: b, s -go-> …, label goal = …) makes every chain a shareable link, with decimals read as exact fractions. Six tabs: Chain (the model drawn with probability-labelled, action-coloured edges), Query (a PCTL box with HEAT-MAPPED per-state probabilities, the exact-fraction answer, expected hitting time, and — for MDPs — the optimal strategy read off), Bounded (P(F≤k target) charted converging up to the unbounded value), Simulate (a live MONTE-CARLO estimate with a 95% confidence band beside the exact answer, plus an animated seeded sample path stepping through the chain), Verify and About. The Verify tab is a genuine DIFFERENTIAL PROOF (16/16): every probability is recomputed THREE structurally-independent ways — the exact rational linear solve, floating-point VALUE ITERATION, and MONTE-CARLO frequency — which must agree on the gallery and hundreds of random chains; the Prob0/Prob1 graph pre-analysis must bracket the exact answers (p=0 ⟺ Prob0, p=1 ⟺ Prob1); the rational solver's residual must be EXACTLY zero; the textbook closed forms must land on the nose; the PCTL dualities (G φ = 1−F¬φ and ¬(P<p) ≡ P≥p) must hold; and for MDPs exact policy iteration is refereed by a BRUTE-FORCE scan of EVERY deterministic policy (max and min) with float value iteration pinned to it. ALSO — v15 TIMED mode, TIMED AUTOMATA (Alur–Dill 1990) — a finite automaton equipped with real-valued CLOCKS that all advance at rate 1, the standard model of real-time systems and the theory behind UPPAAL. Edges carry clock GUARDS (x>=2) and RESETS; locations carry dwell INVARIANTS (x<=5) that force progress. The state space — a location plus a valuation in R^n_{>=0} — is UNCOUNTABLE, yet reachability is decidable, and this mode shows WHY two independent ways that get graded against each other live. First, Alur & Dill's REGION AUTOMATON: two valuations that agree on every clock's integer part (up to its max constant) and on the ORDER of their fractional parts can never be told apart by any guard, now or ever, and stay equivalent as time elapses — so the infinite space has a FINITE time-abstract bisimulation quotient, built here from scratch (region time-successors, resets, the delay chain under invariants) and drawn as the classic two-clock PARTITION OF THE PLANE (corner points, open grid/diagonal segments, open triangles) with the regions reachable at a chosen location lit up. Second, the algorithm real tools actually run — symbolic forward reachability over ZONES carried as DIFFERENCE BOUND MATRICES: a zone is a convex valuation set x_i-x_j<=c stored as an (n+1)x(n+1) matrix over a fictitious zero-clock, where delay (release upper bounds), reset (copy the zero row/column), guard intersection and inclusion are small matrix surgery and the canonical tightest form is Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest paths; to keep the fixpoint finite, zones are widened by maximal-bound EXTRAPOLATION (Extra_M) once a clock passes its largest constant. A live DBM inspector reads each zone back as constraints. A textual syntax (clocks x,y / loc L inv x<=5 / A -> B if x>=2 do x act a) makes every machine a shareable link, a concrete RUN tab drives the ground-truth operational semantics (wait, then take an enabled edge, the deadline shown as the invariant's slack), and the Verify tab is a genuine DIFFERENTIAL PROOF (11/11): the region automaton and the DBM zone fixpoint, which SHARE NO CODE, compute the IDENTICAL set of reachable locations on every gallery machine and 400 random ones; plus the DBM algebra (canonical-form idempotence, emptiness = negative cycle, monotone delay/extrapolation/guard), the region time-successor checked against concrete delay, a three-way concrete-in-region-in-zone soundness cross-check over 1200 sampled configs, a known-answer battery (an invariant beating a guard makes a location UNREACHABLE; relax it and it opens), and parser round-trips. Six tabs (Automaton, Regions with the plane partition, Zones with the DBM inspector, Run, Verify, About). ALSO — v14 QUANT mode, QUANTITATIVE games on graphs: the floor ABOVE parity, where every edge carries an integer weight and the question turns from 'does Player 0 win?' into 'by HOW MUCH?' — the theory that turns reactive synthesis into resource-aware, cost-optimising synthesis. A MEAN-PAYOFF game's value ν(v) is the long-run average edge weight the maximiser (Max, circle) and minimiser (Min, square) settle into; by Ehrenfeucht-Mycielski both players secure it with a single POSITIONAL strategy and it is a RATIONAL with denominator at most n — so this mode reports it EXACTLY as a fraction, never a float. It is computed three structurally-independent ways that must agree: ZWICK-PATERSON value iteration (play the finite k-step game; once k>4n^3W the average f_k(v)/k pins nu(v) and best-rational rounding recovers it exactly), the BRIM-CHATTERJEE-DOYEN-GIMBERT-RASKIN ENERGY fixpoint (the least sufficient initial credit F(v) to keep the running sum >= 0 forever, TOP where impossible; F(v) finite iff nu(v) >= 0, and it yields Max's strategy), and a brute-force ORACLE that enumerates every memoryless strategy pair and reads the eventual cycle's mean, returning the LOWER (max-min) and UPPER (min-max) values separately so positional determinacy is itself a checked fact. An independent CERTIFICATE pins each side's strategy and inspects the cycles (Karp minimum-cycle-mean): Max's region has min-cycle-mean >= 0, and — using the small-denominator gap nu<0 implies nu <= -1/n — a second scaled/shifted energy solve proves Min drives its region strictly below zero; it rejects a corrupted partition. The headline is the classical PARITY -> MEAN-PAYOFF REDUCTION (priority p maps to weight (-1)^p n^p, so the top priority dominates every cycle's sum and the mean's sign is its parity): run on the qualitative Games mode's own parity arenas, the reduced game's winner matches ZIELONKA's solver VERTEX-FOR-VERTEX, tying the new quantitative engine back to the already-proven one. Five tabs (Arena weight editor, Value with exact nu + energy credits + Max's strategy + the live certificate, Parity->MP showing the reduction agree with Zielonka, Verify, About), proven 8/8 against code they share nothing with: value iteration = oracle (exact rationals), max-min = min-max (determinacy), energy sign = value sign, the certificate holds and has teeth, the parity reduction = Zielonka, and shift/scale invariance nu(w+c)=nu(w)+c and nu(kw)=k nu(w). ALSO — v13 ALGEBRA mode, the ALGEBRAIC theory of regular languages — the third leg of the tripod the subject stands on (automata + logic + algebra). Every regular language has a smallest recognising monoid, its SYNTACTIC MONOID M(L), built here from scratch as the TRANSITION MONOID of the minimal complete DFA (BFS over the generators from the identity; the trap is the monoid's zero), with the Cayley table, shortest-word witnesses and the accepting set P = eta(L). From that one finite algebra the mode reads the language's LOGICAL complexity: GREEN'S RELATIONS R, L, J, H from principal ideals drawn as the EGG-BOX (each D=J-class an R-rows x L-columns grid of H-classes, group cells starred), an APERIODICITY test computed three independent ways (element-powers = H-triviality = the stability test m^n = m^{n+1} at n=|M|), and the headline SCHUTZENBERGER THEOREM verdict — L is STAR-FREE iff M(L) is aperiodic iff (McNaughton-Papert / Kamp) L is FIRST-ORDER FO[<] and LTL definable, so this monoid decides whether a language built in Explore could equally have been written in the Logic mode — plus SIMON'S theorem (piecewise-testable iff J-trivial) and the EILENBERG variety ladder, each verdict carrying its witness and counting obstruction. Six tabs (syntactic monoid + Cayley table, egg-box, structure checklist beside the variety ladder, the star-free verdict with the star-free⟺aperiodic⟺counter-free⟺FO[<]⟺LTL chain, a live VERIFY tab, and About), proven 10/10 against code they share nothing with: the monoid axioms incl. full-triple associativity, RECOGNITION (monoid accepts iff the DFA does) and the homomorphism eta(uv)=eta(u)eta(v), Green consistency (R,L refine J; H=R∩L; D=J re-derived as the join of R and L), the three aperiodicity computations agreeing, the egg-box tiling the monoid exactly once, hand-checked known answers (Z/2, Z/3, semilattice, star-free), and a negative control catching a corrupted product. NEWEST — v12 GAMES mode, the floor ABOVE model checking: INFINITE TWO-PLAYER GAMES ON FINITE GRAPHS, the computational engine of the modal MU-CALCULUS and of REACTIVE-CONTROLLER SYNTHESIS (parity games are polynomial-time inter-reducible with mu-calculus model checking, so this is the general machine the lab's LTL/CTL/CTL* checkers are special cases of). A token moves forever along a graph whose vertices are owned by two players; a winning condition decides the infinite play. All four canonical conditions are solved from scratch: REACHABILITY and SAFETY by a single ATTRACTOR least-fixpoint with positional strategy extraction, BUCHI (a liveness condition — an accepting state infinitely often) by the McNaughton/Zielonka peel-off fixpoint, and PARITY (highest priority seen infinitely often is even) by the full MCNAUGHTON-ZIELONKA recursion with two-player memoryless strategy synthesis. Every answer is PROVED by an independent, size-independent CERTIFICATE: pin each winner to its memoryless strategy and — since the opponent now controls all branching — 'can the opponent still win?' collapses to a graph question (a reachable cycle of the wrong parity, via restricted-subgraph Tarjan SCC), so if neither region admits a bad cycle and the two regions cover every vertex the partition is exactly right. Five interactive tabs: an ARENA you edit by clicking (recolour the target/hazard/accepting set, flip an owner, cycle a priority) or roll randomly; a SOLVE tab colouring the winning regions and drawing both positional strategies with a live certificate verdict; a PLAY tab where you take one side and the app answers with the optimal strategy, with loop detection and a per-condition verdict, plus a one-click 'watch both play optimally' lasso; a SYNTHESIS tab that reads Player 0's winning strategy back out as a CONTROLLER TABLE (state -> move) — a provably correct reactive program, the point of Church's synthesis problem; and a VERIFY tab that runs the whole proof harness in the browser. The differential harness proves the engine three independent ways sharing no logic: 1000 random arenas across all four conditions each yield a certificate-proven-exact solution; the fast solvers match a BRUTE-FORCE ORACLE (enumerate every memoryless strategy pair, simulate the deterministic play — the rules and nothing else) vertex-for-vertex on 180 small arenas; direct Buchi equals its parity encoding; parity role-duality (flip owners, shift priorities) swaps the winning regions exactly; and the certificate is shown to have TEETH by rejecting a deliberately corrupted solution; and TWO structurally-independent parity solvers — Zielonka's recursion and JURDZINSKI'S SMALL PROGRESS MEASURES (a least fixpoint over a lattice of tuples over the odd priorities) — are forced to agree on every arena, two famous algorithms sharing no code and one answer. NEWEST — v11 SYMBOLIC mode, a complete from-scratch SYMBOLIC MODEL CHECKER built on a hand-rolled REDUCED ORDERED BINARY DECISION DIAGRAM (ROBDD) engine — the data structure and technique behind SMV/NuSMV that pushed model checking from thousands of states to 10^20 and beyond. The BDD library is the real thing: a hash-consed unique table (canonical nodes, so equal functions share ONE id and equivalence is a pointer compare), the ITE-based Shannon-expansion recursion with a memoized computed table, restriction/cofactor, existential & universal quantification, variable renaming for current↔next bits, EXACT model counting (#SAT) and one-witness extraction. The system is encoded SYMBOLICALLY: a Kripke structure's states become bit-vectors over interleaved current/next variables, the transition relation and every Sat-set become BDDs, and the IDENTICAL Clarke-Emerson-Sistla CTL fixpoints run over BDDs — the pre-image pre∃(Y) as a RELATIONAL PRODUCT (∃ next. T ∧ Y[next]), EU/EF/AF/AU as LEAST and EG/AG/ER/AR as GREATEST fixpoints, convergence detected by a single canonical-id comparison. Three tabs make it tangible: a BDD EXPLORER that compiles any Boolean formula to its ROBDD, draws the decision DAG (hi/lo edges, shared nodes, reduced skips) with a live satisfying-path trace and a truth table, and lets you REORDER the variables to watch the node count swing from linear to exponential — the NP-hard ordering problem made visible; a TRANSITION-RELATION tab showing the symbolic encoding, the relation BDD (far smaller than the naive 2^2k table) and symbolic forward REACHABILITY as an animated μ-fixpoint; and a SYMBOLIC CHECK tab that runs the CTL fixpoints on BDDs, decodes each Sat-set back to state names and highlights it on the model graph, animates each fixpoint's per-round BDD node counts, and — the headline — DECODES the symbolic result and compares it LIVE against the explicit boolean-array checker for the exact model, proving the two engines agree state-for-state. The Verify tab differentially proves the whole engine (7/7) against code it shares NOTHING with: symbolic CTL agrees with the v9 EXPLICIT checker at EVERY state over 250 random (model, formula) pairs (0 mismatches), ITE matches brute-force truth tables, the algebra laws (double-negation, De Morgan, absorption, complement) hold by canonical id-equality, #SAT matches enumeration, the exists/forall identities and witness soundness hold, the propositional parser round-trips, and symbolic reachability equals explicit BFS over 200 models. ALSO — v10 CTL* mode, a complete from-scratch CTL* MODEL CHECKER that closes the temporal-logic hierarchy: CTL* is the logic ABOVE both LTL and CTL, dropping CTL's rule that a path quantifier must hug one temporal operator so E (some path) / A (all paths) bind an ARBITRARY path formula — letting the temporal operators nest freely. E[G F p] ('some path is fair') and A[(G F req) -> (G F ack)] (strong-fairness response) are expressible in NEITHER CTL nor LTL alone; CTL* is exactly the closure that contains them, alongside the linear idiom F G p and the branching idiom A G E F reset. It is checked by the EMERSON-LEI algorithm, which is the genuine SYNTHESIS of the lab's two temporal engines: strip the INNERMOST quantifier, decide E rho ('some path from here satisfies the LTL body rho') by the v8 GPVW/Vardi-Wolper Büchi-automaton emptiness check run per state — and A rho = ¬E¬rho by its dual — name the result with a fresh proposition, substitute upward, and finish on a Boolean residual. So the OUTSIDE is the v9 branching labelling and the INSIDE is the v8 LTL automata, glued by atom introduction. The Decompose tab animates the elimination round by round — each fresh label lighting up its Sat-set on the model graph, with a REPLAYABLE witnessing/refuting lasso per start state — and a Formula tab classifies any formula as linear / CTL / proper CTL*. The live Verify tab differentially proves the whole chain (7/7) against engines that share NO code with the checker: on the CTL fragment the Emerson-Lei checker agrees with the v9 SYMBOLIC-FIXPOINT labelling engine at every state over 700 random (model, formula) pairs (0 mismatches); on full CTL* the production GPVW emptiness agrees with an INDEPENDENT Tarjan-SCC path-existence oracle over 350 pairs (0 mismatches); on the linear fragment A rho / E rho agree with the v8 DIRECT ω-word semantics over 400 pairs; plus the A rho = ¬E¬rho duality, certificate soundness (every witness lasso is a real path replayed under the direct semantics), and every gallery verdict. ALSO — v9 BRANCHING mode, a complete from-scratch CTL MODEL CHECKER that completes the temporal-logic story: where the Logic mode is LINEAR time (one path at a time), Computation Tree Logic reasons about the TREE of futures, pairing every temporal operator with a path quantifier E (some path) or A (all paths) — EX/AX, EF/AF, EG/AG and the bracketed E[a U b]/A[a R b]. It is checked by a completely different algorithm: the LABELLING ALGORITHM of Clarke-Emerson-Sistla, computing Sat(psi) — the set of states where each subformula holds — bottom-up, with the temporal operators as LEAST fixpoints (EU/AU/EF/AF) and GREATEST fixpoints (EG/AG/ER/AR) of a pre-image step, and the Labelling tab ANIMATES the whole approximant chain Z0, Z1, … converging to the fixpoint. It witnesses verdicts with replayable CERTIFICATES — a finite path to a bad state, or a goal-avoiding LASSO — every per-state obligation independently verified, a failing formula certified by the witness of its negation in NNF. The headline properties (AG EF restart — 'from every reachable state the system can be reset', AG EF up — recoverability) are provably INEXPRESSIBLE in LTL, the whole reason branching time earns its own mode; the About tab makes the CTL/LTL incomparability concrete. The live Verify tab differentially proves the chain (7/7): the symbolic fixpoint checker agrees at EVERY state with a SECOND, structurally-independent oracle that decides the operators by explicit backward-BFS reachability and Tarjan SCC analysis — 0 mismatches over 400 random (model, formula) pairs — plus adequacy of the {not, and, EX, EU, EG} rewrite, the textbook fixpoint identities, certificate soundness, and ACTL matching the LTL semantics on linear models. ALSO — v8 LOGIC mode, a complete from-scratch LTL MODEL CHECKER that lifts the lab from finite words to the INFINITE traces of reactive systems. Write a Linear Temporal Logic formula and watch the GPVW TABLEAU (Gerth-Peled-Vardi-Wolper 1995 — the construction inside SPIN's ltl2ba) turn it into a generalized BÜCHI AUTOMATON by unrolling a U b ≡ b ∨ (a ∧ X(aUb)) and a R b ≡ b ∧ (a ∨ X(aRb)), then DEGENERALIZE it (the Baier-Katoen counter construction) to an ordinary Büchi automaton — the ω-word cousin of the NFA — drawn with the app's pan/zoom/export renderer (propositional guards under each state, double-ring accepts, a start arrow per initial state). Build a system as a KRIPKE STRUCTURE in a tiny DSL, then MODEL-CHECK it by the VARDI-WOLPER automata-theoretic method: form the product A(¬φ) ⊗ M, search for a reachable accepting state on a cycle, and get back either a proof the property holds or an ANIMATED LASSO COUNTEREXAMPLE (a stem leading into a forever-repeated loop, with a playhead). An ω-word tracer checks any ultimately-periodic word against both the automaton and an INDEPENDENT direct-semantics oracle, and the live Verify tab differentially proves the whole chain — across 400 random (formula, word) pairs the automaton for φ accepts a word IFF the independent LTL semantics says it satisfies φ (0 mismatches), exactly one of A(φ)/A(¬φ) accepts each word, and every counterexample is replayed as a genuine violating model path. ALSO — v7 Learn mode, a complete from-scratch implementation of ANGLUIN'S L* ACTIVE-LEARNING algorithm: the target machine is HIDDEN and the app must RECONSTRUCT its minimal DFA by asking only membership and equivalence queries — and the teacher is the lab's OWN product-automaton equivalence check, which hands back the shortest distinguishing counterexample. Watch the iconic OBSERVATION TABLE fill in cell by cell (rows coloured by signature, so same colour = same discovered state; closedness defects flagged in the boundary the instant before they are promoted), scrub through every atomic step — each membership bit, each closing and consistency repair, each conjecture and counterexample — toggle between the Angluin-1987 (add every prefix to S) and Rivest-Schapire-1993 (binary-search one distinguishing suffix into E) counterexample rules and see RS use far fewer queries, and watch the hypothesis DFA grow until it provably equals the target, with a live read-out of membership/equivalence query counts. It converges to exactly the Hopcroft-minimal DFA — differential-tested over 16 curated + 400 random targets under both strategies. ALSO — v6 Parse mode, a complete from-scratch PARSER GENERATOR built on the FIRST/FOLLOW engine: the top-down LL(1) predictive table M[A,a] (with conflict detection for left-recursion / common-prefix grammars) and the ENTIRE bottom-up tower LR(0) < SLR(1) < LALR(1) < LR(1) — the canonical item-set automaton (closure/goto, LR(1) lookahead propagation via FIRST(βa), and LALR by core-merging proven to yield exactly |LR(0)| states), drawn with the app's pan/zoom/export renderer; the ACTION/GOTO parse tables with shift-reduce & reduce-reduce conflicts flagged; a live grammar CLASSIFIER (which classes the grammar belongs to, and why the rest fail); and ANIMATED stack-driven parsers — a predictive LL(1) parser building the leftmost tree and a shift-reduce LR parser building the rightmost tree in reverse, both step-scrubbable. A curated gallery puts each grammar on a different rung (Knuth's pointer grammar is LALR(1)-not-SLR(1); the classic reduce/reduce-on-merge grammar is LR(1)-not-LALR(1); dangling-else is an unavoidable shift/reduce). Every parser is differential-tested to accept exactly L(G) against the Earley oracle. REGULAR (level 3): compile a regex into a parse tree, Thompson e-NFA, subset-construction DFA, Hopcroft-minimized DFA and a Brzozowski-derivative DFA; step strings through any of them; compare two regexes via the product automaton (union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference), decide equivalence/containment and prove inequality with the shortest distinguishing string; or draw your own automaton in Build mode, with a Myhill-Nerode table and direct NFA-to-regex. CONTEXT-FREE (level 2) — Grammar mode: analyze a grammar (nullable / generating / reachable / useless, FIRST & FOLLOW), normalize to Chomsky Normal Form step-by-step, recognize strings two ways (CYK table + Earley chart), render the derivation tree with ambiguity detection, sample the language, compile to a pushdown automaton with an animated stack, and play the CFL pumping lemma. NEW in v5 — Machine mode, the TOP of the hierarchy (level 0/1): a single-tape Turing machine simulator with an animated two-way tape, full configuration trace, a state-transition diagram and a delta-table, a linear-bounded (context-sensitive) mode, and a gallery of deciders for languages no grammar can describe — a-n b-n c-n and w#w are NOT context-free yet a TM decides them live — plus transducers, Rado's busy beaver, and a nondeterministic-TM configuration search. Bridges run both ways: every regex becomes a right-linear grammar AND a read-only Turing machine. No libraries — every parser, automaton algorithm, the graph layout and the SVG renderer are hand-written and differential-tested.
